# Intake Brief: Plan/intake skills iterate over children & verify AC coverage

## Problem statement

When the `plan` or `intake` skills run on a work item that has child work items,
they currently process only the target item — they never descend into the
children. This leaves parent/child AC coverage unverified: a parent's acceptance
criteria may not be collectively covered by its children's ACs, and children are
never themselves planned/intaked (so the decomposition tree can be incomplete
or inconsistent at depth).

## Users

- **Agents running `/skill:plan`** on an epic or other parent with children —
  need the skill to recurse over the whole tree so every level is planned, and
  to verify that the union of child ACs covers the parent ACs.
- **Agents running `/skill:intake`** on a parent with children — need intake to
  run per child (when children exist) and to verify cross-level AC coverage.
- **Operators** — get decomposition trees whose ACs are guaranteed (or
  explicitly flagged) to cover their parents, with gaps auto-closed where
  resolvable and hard conflicts surfaced instead of silently passing.

Example user stories:

- As an agent planning an epic with children, I want the plan skill to iterate
  the whole subtree (respecting dependency order) so I don't have to invoke
  `/skill:plan` per child manually.
- As an agent planning a parent, I want a final review step that verifies the
  children's ACs collectively cover the parent's ACs, auto-closing gaps it can
  resolve and stopping with a clear report when it cannot, so a `plan_complete`
  stage is only reached when coverage is guaranteed.
- As an operator re-running intake on a decomposed epic, I want intake to verify
  AC coverage across the existing children (and per child when configured) so
  the tree stays coherent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (tree iteration — plan):** Running `/skill:plan` on a work item with
  children processes the entire subtree, not just the target: the skill
  iterates children (each child's own plan run, recursing to any depth), in
  dependency order first (`wl dep` edges), then listed order. Verified by a
  test with a multi-level tree (parent → children → grandchildren) asserting
  every node is planned and the processing order respects `wl dep` edges.
- **AC2 (tree iteration — intake):** Running `/skill:intake` on a work item
  with children runs intake per child (recursing the subtree) and also verifies
  AC coverage across existing children. Verified by a test where intake on a
  parent with children runs per child and reports coverage.
- **AC3 (collective coverage):** After processing, for every parent node in the
  tree, the union of its children's acceptance criteria collectively covers the
  parent's acceptance criteria (each parent AC is covered by at least one child
  AC). Verified by a coverage-check test with a parent whose ACs are covered
  by children and a negative test where coverage is missing.
- **AC4 (final review step — auto-close & stop):** The skills' final review
  step closes coverage gaps it can resolve unambiguously (e.g. adding a missing
  child AC that directly maps to an uncovered parent AC), and when a gap or
  conflict cannot be resolved, stops and reports rather than advancing
  (`plan_complete`/`intake_complete` not set; item left `open` with a comment
  describing the conflict). Verified by tests: one where an unambiguous gap is
  auto-closed, one where an unresolvable conflict prevents stage advancement.
- **AC5 (docs & tests):** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
  changes (plan SKILL.md, intake SKILL.md, shared helper docstrings), and the
  full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Worklog API only:** read children via `wl show <id> --children --json`;
  dependency edges via `wl dep list <id> --json`. No direct worklog file edits.
- **No work item for the process itself:** the skills must not create a work
  item to track the iteration itself.
- **Idempotence:** re-running must not create duplicate children or duplicate
  comments; existing children are reused/updated per the existing plan-skill
  idempotence rules.
- **Status lifecycle:** all status transitions go through `StatusLifecycle`
  (intake via `intake.py`, plan via `StatusLifecycle.update_status`); the new
  final review step must leave the item in a valid terminal status (`open`,
  `blocked`, or `completed`) even when it stops on an unresolvable conflict.
- **Conservative auto-closing:** only close gaps that are unambiguous (a child
  AC that clearly maps to an uncovered parent AC). Never invent requirements —
  if intent is unclear, record an Open Question / stop instead.
- **Scope:** affects the `plan` and `intake` skills (SKILL.md workflows) and
  their shared helpers. Must not change audit, implement, or other skills'
  behavior. Must not alter the audit skill's parent-child verdict semantics.

## Existing state

- `skill/plan/SKILL.md` decomposes the target into child feature work items;
  it creates children (Process step 7) and runs six automated review stages on
  the freshly generated feature plan, but never recurses into children and has
  no AC-coverage check across the tree. Its "Automated review on existing
  content" path (skip decision) reviews existing content but still does not
  iterate the tree.
- `skill/intake/SKILL.md` prepares a single work item (claim → gather → draft →
  five mini-reviews → find-related → finish). It has no child iteration or
  coverage verification.
- `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py` provides shared autoplan/approval-gate logic;
  it has no tree/coverage helpers.
- `wl` supports `wl show <id> --children --json` and `wl dep list/add/rm`, so
  tree traversal and ordering data are available without new CLI work.
- The audit skill already has parent/child awareness (child stage checks,
  inherited passes) — a useful reference for tree semantics but NOT to be
  modified by this item.

## Desired change

- **Shared helper (new or extended):** a module (e.g.
  `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py` or new functions in `plan_helpers.py`) that:
  1. Fetches the full descendant tree via `wl show <id> --children --json`.
  2. Orders siblings by `wl dep` edges (topological) then listed order.
  3. Extracts ACs from each item's description (`## Acceptance Criteria`
     section).
  4. Computes coverage: for each parent AC, whether any child AC covers it.
  5. Auto-closes unambiguous gaps; returns an explicit list of unresolvable
     conflicts.
- **Plan skill:** add a "tree iteration" step (before/around Process step 7)
  that recurses into children; add a final "AC coverage review" step after the
  six review stages that applies the helper, auto-closes gaps, and on
  unresolvable conflicts stops without advancing the stage (leaving the item
  `open` with a conflict comment).
- **Intake skill:** add a per-child intake pass (when children exist) and a
  final AC-coverage verification step mirroring the plan behavior.
- **Tests:** unit tests for the shared helper (tree fetch/order, AC extraction,
  coverage computation, gap auto-close, conflict detection) plus skill-workflow
  tests asserting stage advancement is blocked on unresolvable conflicts.

## Key Files

- `skill/plan/SKILL.md` — Add tree-iteration and final AC-coverage review steps
  to the Process section.
- `skill/intake/SKILL.md` — Add per-child intake pass and AC-coverage
  verification step.
- `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py` (new) — Shared tree traversal, ordering,
  AC extraction, coverage computation, gap auto-close, conflict detection
  (or equivalent functions added to `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py` if shared
  placement is not preferred).
- `skill/plan/tests/test_plan_helpers.py` — Extend with tree/coverage helper
  tests (or add `skill/shared/tests/test_tree_coverage.py`).
- `skill/intake/tests/` — Workflow tests for per-child intake and coverage
  stop/advance behavior.

## Related work

- `SA-0MRW0G0XZ009TU6E` — Audit runner circular dependency fix; documents the
  audit skill's child-stage semantics (children in `in_review` don't block
  parent closure). Reference only; not to be modified here.
- `SA-0MSK9IOEF007PP5S` — Audit skill: reduce wall-clock time; example of a
  parent item decomposed into children via the plan skill.
- `SA-0MSJI53RX006E2PS` — Reduce initial LLM context; an epic with 6 children,
  useful as a real-world tree for manual validation of the new iteration.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — Already has child-aware logic (recursive child
  implementations, terminal-stage checks); a pattern reference for how skills
  handle trees.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` + `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — Parent/child
  verdict and stage semantics; reference for tree behavior conventions.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: recursion depth/time.** Deep trees could make plan/intake slow or
  loop. Mitigation: recursion bounded by the actual tree; each child processed
  once; idempotent re-runs. Note: no explicit depth cap is assumed unless
  needed — flag in implementation if cycles are possible in worklog trees.
- **Risk: AC extraction brittleness.** Descriptions vary in formatting; ACs may
  be missing or malformed. Mitigation: tolerant extraction; missing ACs treated
  as an uncovered gap reported to the user rather than silently ignored.
- **Risk: auto-closing gaps could invent content.** Mitigation: only
  unambiguous, directly-mapped gaps are auto-closed; everything else stops with
  a report (per AC4).
- **Assumption:** worklog trees are acyclic (a work item's children cannot
  contain it). If a cycle is ever detected, the skill stops and reports.
- **Assumption:** `wl dep list <id> --json` output shape is stable; the helper
  parses both object and array JSON shapes (per existing plan skill guidance).
- **Scope-creep note:** any additional "verify child ACs against parent at
  audit time" ideas are out of scope for this item (audit behavior unchanged)
  and would be tracked as separate work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Should the iteration recurse through the entire tree (a parent with
  children whose children also have children — plan/intake each level), or just
  one level of direct children?" — Answer (user): "entire tree". Final: entire
  tree, any depth.
- Q2: "Does 'run the skill on each dependently' mean respecting the `wl dep`
  dependency edges (topological order — an item only after its prerequisites)?
  Or just sequential order as listed?" — Answer (user): "respect dependencies,
  then order listed". Final: topological order by `wl dep` edges, ties broken
  by listed order.
- Q3: "When the final review finds parent ACs not covered by child ACs, should
  the skill block completion (refuse to advance to `plan_complete`/`intake_complete`
  until fixed or explicitly waived), or report the gaps and continue?" — Answer
  (user): "it should close the gaps. If there is conflict that cannot be
  resolved then stop and report, refusing to advance". Final: auto-close
  unambiguous gaps; unresolvable conflicts stop the skill, item left `open`
  with a report comment, stage not advanced.

  **Answer (producer):** The anser is provided in the question text- Q4: "When intake runs on a parent with children (e.g. re-running on a
  decomposed epic), should it: (a) run intake per child, (b) only verify AC
  coverage across existing children, or (c) both?" — Answer (user): "both".
  Final: intake runs per child AND verifies coverage across existing children.

Source: interactive replies from operator, session 019fe678-68d1-7c92-8723-aeab0ba45cd8.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MRGKZ3QY003498O** – Intake and plan skills should not require CHANGELOG.md updates — handled by ship skill (completed)
- **SA-0MSAIY59V001KECF** – Phase 2: batch child deep analysis into parent call (P6, optional later) (completed)
- **SA-0MS4NWUQC003HWCI** – [MEDIUM] skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py:2019 — Unpacked variable `child_report` is never used (RUF059) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `.worklog/tmp/intake-draft-child-iteration-SA-0MSLRVQIF0040GAM.md` — matched: acceptance, acs, child, children, collectively, cover, coverage, criteria, dependency, dependently, final, intake, item, iterate, one, order, over, parent, plan, respecting, review, run, running, should, skill, skills, step, when, work

# Integration Tests for Plan/Intake Tree Iteration & Coverage

## Problem statement

The audit of SA-0MSLRVQIF0040GAM found that while the shared helper functions (tree_coverage.py) and SKILL.md workflows are well-tested at the unit level, three acceptance criteria (AC1, AC2, AC4) lack end-to-end integration tests that exercise the actual skill mutation behavior:

- **AC1:** No integration test exercises the full plan skill workflow with a multi-level tree (parent → children → grandchildren) asserting end-to-end processing order respects `wl dep` edges.
- **AC2:** No integration test exercises the full intake skill workflow with per-child intake runs and coverage verification.
- **AC4:** No test exercises the actual skill mutation behavior — adding missing child ACs, setting status=open with conflict comments, and blocking stage advancement on unresolvable conflicts.

## Users

- **Agents** running `/skill:plan` on epics with children — need confidence that the tree iteration processes correctly in a multi-level dependency graph.
- **Agents** running `/skill:intake` on decomposed epics — need confidence that per-child intake and coverage verification work as documented.
- **Operators** — need integration test coverage that validates the full workflow, not just the helper functions in isolation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (plan integration):** A test creates a multi-level tree via `wl` commands (parent → 2 children, one child has a grandchild), sets up dependency edges, and runs the plan skill's tree-iteration step (or an equivalent agent-workflow script). The test asserts: every node is processed, the processing order respects `wl dep` edges (topological order with listed-order tie-breaking), and the final stage advancement comment is written.
- **AC2 (intake integration):** A test creates a parent with existing children that have partial AC coverage, runs the intake skill's per-child intake step, and asserts that: each child is processed, coverage is computed across children, and the coverage verification step either auto-closes gaps (when unambiguous) or stops (when conflicts exist).
- **AC3 (mutation behavior — auto-close):** A test simulates an unambiguous coverage gap (parent AC not covered by any child AC, but a clear mapping exists) and asserts that the skill workflow creates/updates a child work item to cover the gap, then advances to `plan_complete`/`intake_complete`.
- **AC4 (mutation behavior — stop on conflict):** A test simulates an unresolvable conflict (parent AC cannot be mapped to any child AC, or mapping would invent requirements) and asserts that: the skill leaves the item in `open` status, writes a comment describing the conflict, and does NOT advance to `plan_complete`/`intake_complete`.
- **AC5 (idempotence):** Re-running the integration test (with the same tree state) does not create duplicate children or duplicate comments, and the final state is identical to the first run.

## Constraints

- Tests must use the Worklog API only (`wl` CLI) — no direct file edits.
- Tests must work against the same worklog backend used in the existing test suite.
- Tests should create and clean up their own work items (ephemeral test tree).
- Must not modify or depend on audit, implement, or other skills' behavior.
- Must not alter the audit skill's parent-child verdict semantics.

## Key Files

- `skill/shared/tests/test_tree_coverage.py` — Extend with integration-level tree workflow tests (or add `skill/shared/tests/test_plan_integration.py` / `skill/shared/tests/test_intake_integration.py` if a separate file is preferred).
- `skill/plan/SKILL.md` — Reference for expected processing order and mutation behavior.
- `skill/intake/SKILL.md` — Reference for expected per-child intake and coverage verification.

## Related work

- Parent: SA-0MSLRVQIF0040GAM — Plan/intake skills: iterate over children, ensure child ACs collectively cover parent ACs (in_review).
- SA-0MRW0G0XZ009TU6E — Audit runner circular dependency fix; reference for tree semantics.
data.title: Add integration tests for plan/intake tree iteration and coverage mutation

# Implementation: per-audit target root on _AuditContext

**Parent:** SA-0MSRLECW2001AA15 — Audit runner: make TARGET_PROJECT_ROOT per-audit dynamic

## Goal

Introduce a per-audit target project root field on `_AuditContext`, resolve it once in `_phase_gate` from the worklog-derived owning root (falling back to the worktree checkout when the launch cwd is the same git repository), and thread it to every residual `TARGET_PROJECT_ROOT` consumer.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Add a `per_audit_project_root: str` field to `_AuditContext` dataclass.
2. In `_phase_gate`, resolve the per-audit root using the same logic as `git_root`: the owning root is the default; when the launch cwd is the same git repository (worktree or own checkout), use `TARGET_PROJECT_ROOT` (the worktree checkout). Store on `ctx.per_audit_project_root`.
3. Thread `per_audit_project_root` (via `ctx.per_audit_project_root` or local alias) to all residual consumers:
   - code-quality scan: `run_code_quality(project_root=per_audit_root, ...)` at audit_runner.py:9367
   - remediation loop: `project_root=per_audit_root` at audit_runner.py:9436
   - `_repo_index` git-failure fallback: take a `project_root` parameter, use per-audit root for `iterdir()` fallback at audit_runner.py:4612-4620
   - debug-log directory: `_debug_log_dir()` derives slug from per-audit root at audit_runner.py:5483-5505
   - F3 suite-execution cwd: `_auto_green_run_outcome(runner, cwd=per_audit_root)` at audit_runner.py:8420
   - F3 test-skill execution: `_run_tests_via_test_skill(cwd=per_audit_root, ...)` at audit_runner.py:8458
4. Retain the module-level `TARGET_PROJECT_ROOT` as the cwd-derived fallback so the existing suite's 40 overrides keep working.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_AuditContext` dataclass, `_phase_gate`, consumers

## Dependencies

- None — pure implementation task

# Implementation: invert the launch-context guard

**Parent:** SA-0MSRLECW2001AA15 — Audit runner: make TARGET_PROJECT_ROOT per-audit dynamic

## Goal

Invert the launch-context guard: replace the abort for a determinable non-owning cwd with a one-line stderr warning (naming the launch root and the owning root); keep the abort for undeterminable ownership only.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `_verify_launch_context` is modified so that when the launch cwd differs from the owning root but ownership IS determinable (explicit --worklog-dir, or prefix-to-sibling match, or worktree convention), it emits a one-line stderr warning and returns `None` (proceed) instead of an error.
2. When ownership is undeterminable (no --worklog-dir, unknown prefix, no sibling match), it still returns the fatal error and the guard in `_phase_gate` still aborts.
3. The warning is emitted to stderr (not the persisted report) so it never perturbs verdicts or JSON output.
4. A launch from the owning project root (or a worktree of the owning project) proceeds silently — no warning emitted.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_verify_launch_context`, `_phase_gate`

## Dependencies

- None — pure implementation task

# Documentation: rewrite scope semantics

**Parent:** SA-0MSRLECW2001AA15 — Audit runner: make TARGET_PROJECT_ROOT per-audit dynamic

## Goal

Rewrite all documentation to reflect the inverted launch-context guard semantics and the per-audit root being used by all consumers.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — rewrite the "Fail-Fast Launch Contract" section (lines ~56-95): a foreign-cwd launch with a determinable owner no longer aborts; the per-audit root is used by all consumers; only undeterminable ownership fails fast.
2. `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — rewrite the scope-semantics section (lines ~368-425): update the table describing launch-context behaviour; update the "remaining TARGET_PROJECT_ROOT consumers" notes (lines ~700-708) to state they are now per-audit.
3. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Dependencies

- None — documentation task, can be done in parallel

# Cascade children of an audit-approved parent to completed/done

**Recurring defect — producer has raised this repeatedly.** Policy restated by the producer (2026-10-02): *if a parent is marked `completed` and it has been audited, then all its children are considered complete.* The concrete fix requested: **when a parent's audit passes, set its children to `status=completed, stage=done`.**

## Problem statement

When the audit runner records a passing verdict for a parent work item, its descendants are left in whatever terminal or non-terminal state they previously held. This lets a parent reach `status=completed, stage=in_review` with a passing audit while its children remain `open`/`blocked`/`in_progress` (or already `done`), so downstream steps can neither treat the subtree as consistent nor close the parent without a manual `wl close --force` sweep.

## Users and user stories

- **Primary user — release producer.** As a producer, when I audit a parent work item and the audit passes, I want every descendant to be marked `completed`/`done` automatically so that I never have to force-close the parent and sweep unfinished children as a side effect.
- **Secondary user — the ship pipeline (`closeWorkItemsAfterRelease`).** As the post-release close step, I want an audit-approved parent's descendants to already be terminal so the collateral-descendant guard does not falsely refuse to close released items.
- **Secondary user — audit operators/agents.** As an audit operator, I want the cascade to be idempotent and authorised only by a passing parent audit, so reruns and failed audits never resurrect or mutate work.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Cascade on passing parent audit.** When the audit runner records a passing verdict for a parent item (`readyToClose === true`, i.e. `ctx.audit_verdict == "yes"` on the success path), every descendant is set to `status=completed, stage=done`, and each cascaded child receives an explanatory comment naming the authorising parent and the audit timestamp.
- [ ] **AC2 — Idempotent and `deleted`-safe.** Re-running the cascade on an already-terminal tree produces no further mutations or duplicate comments; `deleted` descendants are skipped; the cascade never resurrects or re-opens anything.
- [ ] **AC3 — No cascade without a passing audit.** A parent audit that fails (`Ready to close: No`), is fallback-tainted, or has not been run performs **no** cascade and leaves descendants untouched. Cascading is authorised by a passing audit verdict only — never by status/stage alone.
- [ ] **AC4 — Ship close step closes the parent without a refusal.** `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease` closes a parent whose descendants are all terminal (`done`/`deleted`) without a refusal, covered by unit tests that inject `getCandidateItemsFn`/`getDescendantsFn` (overlaps SA-0MUJKPDAA002VVDP tasks).
- [ ] **AC5 — Regression tests cover the behaviour.** Passing-parent → children done (with comments); failing-parent → children untouched; parent with a mix of `deleted`/`done`/`open` children → only the appropriate action; cascade rerun → no further mutation (testing/validation criterion).
- [ ] **AC6 — Existing audit and ship suites pass.** The existing audit runner and ship suites pass and `npm run build` passes.
- [ ] **AC7 — Documentation updated.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (e.g. `skill/audit/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, `docs/dev/release-process.md` as applicable).
- [ ] **AC8 — Full project test suite passes.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
- [ ] **AC9 — Recurrence: audit-ready parents close without a false refusal (SA-0MUR7Y3BJ004FGPP recurrence).** When a parent's audit is recorded outside the audit runner (manual `wl audit-set`) and its descendants are non-terminal, the ship close step cascades the descendants to `completed`/`done` and closes the parent, authorised only by the passing audit verdict (`readyToClose === true`); a non-passing audit still refuses. Referenced by child SA-0MUZIRQ4K004YCGJ.

## Constraints

- The cascade must live where the verdict is known — the parent audit success path in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — not only as a special case inside the ship close step.
- Any `wl` mutations must respect the `StatusLifecycle` claim invariant (an item must be `in_progress` before mutation) and route `--worklog-dir` through the shared resolution helpers so the cascade targets the item's own worklog store regardless of cwd.
- The cascade must not weaken the existing scope guard (SA-0MU2OY1N9000XL2H): a parent whose audit has **not** passed must still refuse to close over non-terminal descendants.
- Must remain safe under dry-run (`--do-not-persist`): a dry-run passing verdict must not mutate descendants.

## Existing state

- **Verdict knowledge.** `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` computes the parent verdict at `audit_verdict = _parse_ready_to_close(report)` (~line 11363) and, in the terminal transition block, takes the `elif ctx.audit_verdict == "yes":` branch (~line 11773) to run `wl update <id> --status completed --stage in_review` (or `--stage done` when already done). This is the natural single point to trigger the cascade.
- **Child-state checks today.** `_check_children_stages` / related helpers already classify children in `in_review`/`done` as exempt but do **not** mutate them; `inherited_pass` records a verdict reuse but never sets `completed`/`done`.
- **Ship close step.** `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease` in `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` (~line 370) computes `candidateIds` from `getCandidateItems()` (= `stage=in_review` only) and refuses a `--force` close when `collateral = descendants.filter(id => !candidateIds.has(id))` is non-empty (~line 534). Descendants already `stage=done` therefore always appear as collateral — tracked narrowly as SA-0MUJKPDAA002VVDP.
- **Evidence (TCE v0.1.19 release, 2026-10-02).** Five parents sat at `completed/in_review` after the release, all audit-approved; the close step refused all five (25 open/blocked children on two of them), and all five had to be closed with `wl close --force`, sweeping 50 descendants to `done`.

## Desired change

1. Add a cascade helper (e.g. `_cascade_descendants_terminal`) in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` that, given a parent id and audit timestamp, walks descendants (`wl show <id> --children` recursively or the existing tree helpers), skips `deleted` and already `completed`/`done` items, and for each remaining descendant issues `wl update <child> --status completed --stage done`, followed by `wl comment add <child>` with a reason naming the parent and audit timestamp.
2. Invoke the helper from the `ctx.audit_verdict == "yes"` success branch only (and not on the failure/fallback restore branches), after the parent's own verified transition succeeds; suppress it under dry-run.
3. Make the helper idempotent (no mutation/comment when a child is already terminal) and non-fatal (a cascade failure for one child is logged and does not abort the audit, matching the ship step's non-blocking semantics).
4. Keep `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease`'s collateral logic unchanged apart from SA-0MUJKPDAA002VVDP's `done`/`deleted` exclusion (defence-in-depth).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — Add the cascade helper and call it on the `ctx.audit_verdict == "yes"` success path; reuse existing descendant/`_run_wl` helpers.
- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — Ensure `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease` excludes terminal (`done`/`deleted`) descendants from `collateral` (SA-0MUJKPDAA002VVDP); add/verify injected-fn unit coverage for AC4.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_children.py` — New cascade regression tests (passing parent, failing parent, mixed child states, idempotent rerun, dry-run).
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py` — Extend lifecycle-transition tests to assert cascade/no-cascade per verdict.
- `tests/unit/test-close-work-items-after-release.mjs` — Unit tests for the terminal-descendant non-refusal (AC4).
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, `docs/dev/release-process.md` — Document cascade-on-audit behaviour (AC7).

## Related work

- **SA-0MUJKPDAA002VVDP** (open) — "Ship close step falsely refuses to close released items whose descendants are already `stage=done`": the narrower ship-side workaround. This item is the root-cause counterpart; they should be implemented together (or this item's AC1–AC3 makes the ship-side workaround unnecessary, keeping SA-0MUJKPDAA002VVDP as defence-in-depth).
- **SA-0MUA4Q431008HIH0** (in-progress) — "Audit runner: pre-review child with `inherited_pass` bypasses children-stage block and summary claims all children in `in_review`/`done`": the likely mechanism by which parents reach `in_review` with open children; fixing it prevents the "unfinished children under a done parent" failure mode.
- **SA-0MQFXVJAZ004A29L** (completed) — "wl close should recursively close children if in-review and audit OK": the original decision; cascade-on-audit is the missing enforcement.
- **SA-0MQIQQ164007HEAA** (completed) — "Parent audit should pass when all children's ACs are met".
- **SA-0MSKB6VJA005N43F** (completed) — "Audit: parent-first child pass-through".
- **SA-0MU2OY1N9000XL2H** (completed) — the scope guard that must not regress.
- **SA-0MSQJABHZ0018APE** (completed) — "Content-gate child verdict reuse in parent audits" (automated find-related match).
- **SA-0MSABZO2T004B95X** (completed) — "Audit runner: make cumulative elapsed-time guard configurable" (automated find-related match).
- **Provenance:** filed from the Tableau-Card-Engine v0.1.19 release retro (2026-10-02).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — scope creep into the ship step.** The root fix is audit-side; touching `run-release.js` beyond the terminal-descendant exclusion risks duplicating SA-0MUJKPDAA002VVDP. Mitigation: keep the ship change minimal and additive.
- **Risk — partial cascade on `wl` failure.** A mid-cascade `wl` failure could leave a subtree half-terminal. Mitigation: per-child try/except, loud logging, idempotent rerun, non-fatal semantics; the next audit success completes the cascade.
- **Risk — comment noise / non-idempotence.** Re-auditing a passing parent must not duplicate comments. Mitigation: skip already-terminal children before commenting; test the rerun path (AC2/AC5).
- **Risk — regression to the audit scope guard.** Cascading on a *failed* verdict would bypass SA-0MU2OY1N9000XL2H. Mitigation: cascade only on the `audit_verdict == "yes"` branch; explicit failing-parent test (AC3/AC5).
- **Assumption.** "Descendants" means the full recursive subtree of the audited parent (children, grandchildren, …), consistent with `wl close --force`'s recursive sweep.
- **Assumption.** A passing parent audit is the sole authorisation signal; `status`/`stage` alone never authorises a cascade.
- **Assumption.** `deleted` descendants are historical and must never be re-marked or commented on.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q:** Are any clarifications required beyond the seed context? — **Answer (producer, via the filed work item SA-0MUR7Y3BJ004FGPP and the TCE v0.1.19 release retro, 2026-10-02):** No. The seed context specifies the policy, the concrete requested fix ("when a parent's audit passes, set its children to `completed`/`done`"), the desired behaviour (5 points), the acceptance criteria, and the related work. The interview was therefore skipped per the intake "seed context suffices" rule.
- **Q:** Where should the cascade live? — **Answer (producer, seed context, Desired behaviour §2):** In `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` on the parent audit success path — a single source of truth where the verdict is known — not only as a special case in the ship close step. Evidence: repository inspection confirms the `ctx.audit_verdict == "yes"` branch (~`audit_runner.py:11773`) is the success transition point.
- **Q:** How should `deleted` and already-terminal descendants be treated? — **Answer (producer, seed context, Desired behaviour §3):** `deleted` children are left untouched; reruns are no-ops; the cascade never resurrects or re-opens anything.

# Ship close fallback: cascade descendants of an audit-ready parent (recurrence)

Parent: **SA-0MUR7Y3BJ004FGPP** — *Cascade children of an audit-approved parent to completed/done*.

## Why

The original fix cascaded descendants only on the audit runner's verified
`ctx.audit_verdict == "yes"` success path (`_cascade_descendants_terminal`).
The 2026-10-08 AI_Hell v0.1.10 release showed the third recurrence: two
top-level parents were audit-ready (`readyToClose=true`) but their audits had
been recorded **outside** the runner (`wl audit-set` / manual approval, no
fingerprint/rawOutput), so the cascade never fired. `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease`
then refused to `--force`-close them because their descendants were still
non-terminal (`open`/`blocked`), leaving audit-ready items stuck `in_review`.

`wl audit-set` lives in the external worklog CLI, so the audit-side path cannot
intercept a manual approval from this repository. The robust in-repo fix is a
**ship-side fallback**: when a release candidate parent is audit-ready but has
non-terminal descendants, cascade those descendants (authorised by the parent's
passing audit) and then close the parent.

## Goal

As a release producer, when a released parent is audit-ready but has
non-terminal descendants (because its audit was recorded outside the runner),
I want the ship close step to cascade them to `completed`/`done` and close the
parent, rather than refusing and leaving it `in_review` forever.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Cascade on audit-ready parent.** In `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease`,
  when a candidate's non-terminal collateral descendants exist AND the
  candidate's audit is passing (`readyToClose === true`), each non-terminal
  descendant is set to `status=completed, stage=done` with an explanatory
  comment naming the authorising parent and the audit timestamp; the parent is
  then closed (no refusal).
- [ ] **AC2 — No cascade without a passing audit.** When the candidate's audit
  is missing, not passing (`readyToClose !== true`), or transient, no cascade
  occurs and the existing refusal over non-terminal descendants is retained
  (scope guard SA-0MU2OY1N9000XL2H preserved).
- [ ] **AC3 — Dry-run safe.** Under `dryRun`, the intended cascade is reported
  but no `wl update`/`wl comment` mutation is performed.
- [ ] **AC4 — Idempotent / terminal-safe.** Descendants already terminal
  (`stage=done`) or `deleted` are never cascaded or commented on.
- [ ] **AC5 — Regression tests.** Tests inject
  `getCandidateItemsFn`/`getDescendantsFn`/`getItemLifecycleFn` and cascade/audit
  fns and assert on captured arguments — no live worklog mutation. Cases:
  passing parent → descendants cascaded + parent closed; failing/missing audit →
  no cascade + refused; dry-run → no mutation; already-terminal → no cascade.
- [ ] **AC6 — Documentation updated.** `skill/ship/SKILL.md` (or the relevant
  ship docs) and `docs/dev/release-process.md` describe the fallback cascade.
- [ ] **AC7 — Build and full suite pass.** `npm run build` and the full project
  test suite pass.

## Scope / key files

- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — add the fallback cascade to
  `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease` (new injectable `getParentAuditFn` /
  `runCascadeCommand` hooks; default implementations shell out to
  `wl audit-show`, `wl update`, `wl comment add`).
- `tests/unit/test-close-work-items-after-release.mjs` — regression coverage.
- `skill/ship/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/release-process.md` — documentation.

## Constraints

- Keep the scope guard intact: a parent whose audit has **not** passed must
  still refuse to close over non-terminal descendants.
- Cascade authorised by the passing audit verdict only — never by status/stage.
- Non-fatal per child, matching the audit-side cascade semantics.
- Do not duplicate the audit-side fix; this is the defence-in-depth/fallback.

# SorraAgents: decide fate of untracked `skill/pane-triage`

**Headline:** Make the deployed `pane-triage` global skill a tracked, hygiene-compliant member of `SorraAgents/skill` (Option A) instead of leaving it as a locally-excluded untracked copy, so `/skill:pane-triage` is reproducible from a fresh clone and the skill inventory, description-hygiene, and context-budget gates all agree.

## Problem Statement

The SorraAgents main checkout carries a **permanently untracked**
`skill/pane-triage/` directory (locally excluded via `.git/info/exclude`) that is
a deployed copy of the tracked `skill/pane-triage/` in ContextHub. Because
`~/.pi/agent/skills` is a symlink to `SorraAgents/skill`, this copy is what makes
`/skill:pane-triage` available to every pi session, yet it is invisible to a
fresh clone, is excluded from the skill inventory/budget, and (before the
untracked-dir isolation work) failed the hygiene and context-budget gates. A
decision is required: make the skill a first-class tracked global skill in
SorraAgents, or remove the copy.

## Users

- **Producer / operator** — relies on `/skill:pane-triage` to review and close
  idle herdr panes; a removal would silently retire the skill for every
  framework project whose global skills resolve to `SorraAgents/skill`.
  - *As a producer, I want `/skill:pane-triage` to keep working after a fresh
    `git clone` of SorraAgents, so my pane-cleanup workflow is reproducible on
    any machine.*
- **Framework maintainer** — needs the global skill inventory, description
  hygiene, and startup context-budget gate to reflect reality, so an untracked
  directory cannot hide a skill or skew the counts.
  - *As a maintainer, I want every global skill tracked in SorraAgents, so the
    hygiene tests, context-budget thresholds, and install script agree on the
    same skill set.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **The skill is tracked.** `git ls-files skill/pane-triage` in the SorraAgents
   repository lists `SKILL.md`, `__init__.py`, `scripts/pane-triage.py`,
   `scripts/pane_triage.py`, and `tests/test_pane_triage.py`; the
   `skill/pane-triage/` entry is removed from `.git/info/exclude`; a fresh
   checkout of `dev` contains `skill/pane-triage/SKILL.md`.
2. **Doc hygiene passes.** `skill/pane-triage/SKILL.md` passes
   `tests/test_skill_path_conventions.py` (no legacy `skill/<name>/` references
   and no CWD-relative script invocations — commands use
   `$(skill_path pane-triage)/scripts/...`) and
   `tests/test_skill_description_hygiene.py` (frontmatter description ≤140 chars,
   contains "Use when", starts with an action word). `pane-triage` is added to
   `NON_WORK_ITEM_SKILLS` in `tests/test_report_wiring_hygiene.py` (it creates or
   updates no work items, so it must not carry the standardized-report final
   step).
3. **Inventory and budget agree.** The expectations in
   `tests/test_skill_description_hygiene.py` are updated for the new tracked
   skill count and total-prose budget (and the reduction-baseline exclusions, if
   applicable); `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` is regenerated with
   `--include-hidden`; `docs/dev/context-budget.md` records a dated bump note
   with justification.
4. **Source parity (no drift).** The ContextHub source `skill/pane-triage/`
   receives the same hygiene edits so the deployed copy and the source do not
   diverge; the tracking/deployment model is documented in
   `docs/pane-triage-skill.md` (ContextHub).
5. **Verification.** The targeted hygiene/context-budget tests
   (`test_skill_description_hygiene.py`, `test_report_wiring_hygiene.py`,
   `test_skill_path_conventions.py`, `test_context_budget_gate.py`,
   `test_pre_push_context_budget_gate.py`) pass with the directory tracked, and
   the context-budget pre-push gate passes on `dev`.
6. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. **Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Repo boundary.** Global skills live in `SorraAgents/skill/` (symlinked to
  `~/.pi/agent/skills` by `SorraAgents/scripts/install_pi.sh`); the `WL-` work
  item is tracked in ContextHub's worklog and its code lands in SorraAgents
  `dev`. This mirrors the machine-hygiene epic (`WL-0MUJLCVRS0093EJJ`).
- **Do not weaken the untracked-dir isolation work.** The filters added by
  `SA-0MUQ96V5W000TMTU` / `SA-0MUU206QT001M66F` / `SA-0MUPDDMXB0088CMM` must
  stay: concurrent agents' genuinely transient `skill/<name>/` WIP must remain
  ignorable. This item removes the *permanent* untracked directory, it does not
  remove the general guard.
- **Runtime dependency is unchanged.** The skill shells out to the ContextHub
  compiled bridge (`packages/herdr/dist/pane-close-cli.js`) via
  `CONTEXTHUB_DIR`/`PANE_TRIAGE_BRIDGE`; committing the Python copy to
  SorraAgents does not move that dependency.
- **No behaviour change** to the skill's classification, approval gate, or
  never-close guards — this is a tracking/hygiene fix only.

## Existing State

- `SorraAgents/skill/pane-triage/` exists and is byte-identical (source files)
  to `ContextHub/skill/pane-triage/`; only `__pycache__/*.pyc` differ.
- The SorraAgents copy is excluded locally by `.git/info/exclude`
  (`skill/pane-triage/`) and is therefore untracked.
- `tests/test_skill_description_hygiene.py` expects exactly 19 tracked skills;
  `tests/test_report_wiring_hygiene.py` enumerates the expected skill set from
  `WORK_ITEM_SKILLS + NON_WORK_ITEM_SKILLS + ["report"]`.
- The current 140-char description limit is exceeded by the existing 234-char
  `pane-triage` description, and its `SKILL.md` uses `cd $(skill_path
  pane-triage)` + `./scripts/pane-triage.py` invocations.
- The context-budget gate (`measure_context.py --include-hidden`) currently
  passes because untracked dirs are filtered; committing the directory makes it
  count toward `skills_prose`/`total`.

## Desired Change

Choose **Option A — track the skill in SorraAgents** and make it hygiene-compliant:

1. Move `skill/pane-triage/` from untracked/excluded to tracked in SorraAgents
   `dev`, committing the same files that currently make `/skill:pane-triage`
   work.
2. Sanitise `SKILL.md` for the doc-convention and description-hygiene tests:
   rewrite the frontmatter description to ≤140 chars with a "Use when" clause
   and an action-verb first word; replace the `cd $(skill_path pane-triage); ./scripts/...`
   invocation block with `$(skill_path pane-triage)/scripts/...` forms.
3. Register the skill in `NON_WORK_ITEM_SKILLS`
   (`tests/test_report_wiring_hygiene.py`) and update the count/total-prose
   expectations (`tests/test_skill_description_hygiene.py`).
4. Regenerate `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` and add a dated bump
   note to `docs/dev/context-budget.md`.
5. Mirror the `SKILL.md` hygiene edits into the ContextHub source copy and
   document the source/deployment relationship in `docs/pane-triage-skill.md`.

The alternative (**Option B — remove the untracked copy**) is rejected: because
SorraAgents is the sole source of the global skills symlink, removing the copy
would silently retire `/skill:pane-triage` for every framework project while the
skill remains documented and referenced as deployed. Retiring the skill is a
materially larger product decision that should be raised separately if desired.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/pane-triage/SKILL.md` — rewrite description (≤140 chars, "Use when") and script-invocation forms.
- `skill/pane-triage/__init__.py`, `skill/pane-triage/scripts/pane-triage.py`, `skill/pane-triage/scripts/pane_triage.py`, `skill/pane-triage/tests/test_pane_triage.py` — new tracked files (SorraAgents).
- `tests/test_skill_description_hygiene.py` — update expected skill count and total-prose budget.
- `tests/test_report_wiring_hygiene.py` — add `pane-triage` to `NON_WORK_ITEM_SKILLS`.
- `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` — regenerate with `--include-hidden`.
- `docs/dev/context-budget.md` — dated threshold bump note.
- `.git/info/exclude` — remove the `skill/pane-triage/` entry (local, untracked).
- `ContextHub/skill/pane-triage/SKILL.md` — mirror the hygiene edits (source parity).
- `ContextHub/docs/pane-triage-skill.md` — document the tracking/deployment model.

## Risks and Assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk (highest):** committing the skill pulls in a mandatory
  `SKILL.md` rewrite, two hygiene-list/test updates, and a context-budget
  threshold regeneration. Extra opportunities (e.g. retiring the ContextHub
  duplicate, generalising untracked-dir sync) must be recorded as linked work
  items, not absorbed here.
- **Drift risk:** editing only the SorraAgents copy leaves the ContextHub source
  divergent; AC4 mandates mirroring the edits and documenting the relationship.
- **Gate-weakening risk:** the fix must not delete the untracked-dir isolation
  filters; a genuinely transient WIP directory must stay ignorable.
- **Regression risk:** the skill's runtime bridge lives in ContextHub; the
  commit must not alter the `CONTEXTHUB_DIR`/`PANE_TRIAGE_BRIDGE` resolution or
  the approval gate.
- **Assumption:** the deployed copy is the intended artifact (not accidental) —
  supported by `docs/pane-triage-skill.md` and the active global registration.
- **Assumption:** ContextHub remains the source-of-truth repo for the skill and
  the deployed SorraAgents copy is a mirror.

## Related Work

- `WL-0MUJMXVPO0016DZM` — Create pane-triage skill (the skill itself; records the
  "skills are Python-only (`SorraAgents/skill/`)" placement decision).
- `WL-0MUJLCVRS0093EJJ` — machine-hygiene epic; surfaced this untracked copy and
  established the global-skill → SorraAgents commit precedent.
- `SA-0MUQ96V5W000TMTU` / `SA-0MUU206QT001M66F` / `SA-0MUPDDMXB0088CMM` —
  untracked-skill-dir isolation (the guard that must not be weakened).
- `WL-0MUJW9EEP009Q0V3` — shared classifier + automatic reaper (runtime
  dependency of the skill).
- `WL-0MUJW9FY5008KBTQ` — coordinate pane-triage reuse and document closure.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q (agent, evidence-based determination):** Commit the untracked
  `skill/pane-triage` to SorraAgents, or remove it? — **Answer (agent, derived
  from repo evidence):** Commit (Option A). Evidence:
  `ContextHub/docs/pane-triage-skill.md` states the skill is "tracked in
  ContextHub; deployed to the global skills directory as `/skill:pane-triage`";
  `SorraAgents/scripts/install_pi.sh` symlinks `~/.pi/agent/skills` →
  `SorraAgents/skill`, so SorraAgents is the only source of global skills; the
  producer recorded that "skills are Python-only (`SorraAgents/skill/`)" in
  `WL-0MUJMXVPO0016DZM`; and `WL-0MUJLCVRS0093EJJ` established the precedent that
  global skills must be committed in SorraAgents. Removing the copy would break
  `/skill:pane-triage` globally. Source: repo inspection + worklog evidence.
- **OPEN QUESTION (producer confirmation):** Option A is a design decision for a
  tracked global skill, not merely a cleanup. Please confirm during review, or
  raise Option B (retire `/skill:pane-triage`) as a separate work item. Context:
  no producer response was available in this intake session.
- **Q (scope):** Should the redundant ContextHub `skill/pane-triage/` copy be
  removed? — **Answer (assumed):** No — keep ContextHub as the documented
  source-of-truth and mirror the hygiene edits (AC4); removing it would change
  ContextHub's context-budget surface and tests and is out of scope. Recorded as
  an assumption.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MSM3STQ0008QUMG** – [test-failure] should have no legacy skill/ path references (Skill: cleanup) — failing test (completed)
- **WL-0MR24H2VK004PAQ7** – 1a: Error Classification & Settings (tests) (completed)
- **WL-0MKVTAH8S1CQIHP6** – Clicking a work item in TUI tree view does not update/select it in detail pane (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: agent, breaks, budget, byte, checkout (+39 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: agent, budget, byte, checkout, commit (+36 more)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: agent, breaks, budget, checkout, commit (+35 more)
